reading.scope: Physical pages 2–14 read in full, including the start of references on final selected page. Page 1 abstract read separately; remaining reference pages unread. Four page images viewed. No downloaded program execution.

limitations: Linux 6.6 process checkpoint/restore and Docker/OpenWhisk CXLporter, not Firecracker microVM or GPU-state checkpointing. Same OS image and shared filesystem/path assumptions; shared anonymous mappings unsupported.

One dual-socket Sapphire Rapids host, two VMs and Agilex 7 FPGA with 16 GB DDR4 model two nodes. Mitosis-CXL comparison uses one VM with memory copies replacing RDMA; not a real multi-host production fabric.
Checkpoint creation copies data into CXL and serializes global state. Restore maps read-only checkpoint data and later writes copy locally; minimal serialization is not no serialization.

Standalone restore/first execution excludes checkpointing and containers. Burst experiments include ghost-container effects for CXLfork/Mitosis but not CRIU-CXL; do not attribute all P99 gains solely to CXL direct mapping.
Ghost containers occupy 512 KB each in the paper; introductory no-memory language is not literal. Reported local-memory reductions exclude shared CXL footprint.
Page 7 distinguishes OS-managed A-bit updates from page 8 hardware page-walk updates and user resets; the checkpoint is not wholly immutable metadata at every level.
Large-node scalability and shared CXL bandwidth were not evaluated. Latency sensitivity uses calibrated QEMU/SST simulation. No current E2B deployment, kernel execution or author artifact audit.
